sentences.text: Gobihadros is classified as a medium-sized hadrosauroid dinosaur.
It belongs to the superfamily Hadrosauroidea in a basal position outside the family Hadrosauridae.
This species is distinguished from other non-hadrosaurid hadrosauroids by having a double-layered tomial edge on the premaxilla and up to three teeth per position in the lower jaw.
Gobihadros possesses a conical, spike-like claw on its first finger, a trait not found in Tethyshadros, Plesiohadros, or Hadrosauridae.
Life Science Identifiers were required to validate the name Gobihadros because the description was published in an electronic journal.
CT scans of a large individual revealed calcium pyrophosphate deposition disease in its tail vertebrae and foot bones.
The species Gobihadros mongoliensis was formally named and described in 2019 by Khishigjav Tsogtbaatar, David Bruce Weishampel, David Christopher Evans, and Mahito Watabe.
The holotype specimen MPC-D100/746 was discovered in the Bayan Shireh Formation from the Cenomanian-Santonian stages.
Fossils of Gobihadros have been found in what is now Asia.
Researchers suggest the calcium pyrophosphate deposition disease found in this dinosaur likely resulted from old age rather than physical trauma.
Gobihadros lived during the mid-Cretaceous period, approximately between 100.5 and 83.6 million years ago.
The largest known fully grown individual of Gobihadros reached an estimated length of 7.5 meters.
